'''MdZ-BLK''', nicknamed '''Blockhead''', was a [[MdZ series droid]].

==Biography==
===Never underestimate a droid===
MdZ-BLK was an [[MdZ series droid]] manufactured by [[TTC]]<ref name="Cracken" /> sometime before [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]].<ref name="Date">''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]'' established that MdZ-BLK and [[Aimi Loto]] had partnered together for "[[Standard year/Legends|years]]" by the time shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], which equates to at least [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]].</ref> The [[Droid/Legends|droid]] was owned by various individuals, underwent multiple [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipes]], and eventually earned the nickname "Blockhead." He eventually came under ownership of the [[Seville Family|Seville pirate clan]] through employment by its [[Matriarch/Legends|matriarch]], [[Darion Seville]]. Seville sought entertainment by organizing duels between droids, favoring non-combatant droids in particular.<ref name="Cracken" /> 

MdZ-BLK maintained a perfect record during his [[Gladiator droid/Legends|participation]]. He regularly fought against [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droids]] and developed a hatred for the model as a result. Dissatisfied with the arrangement, MdZ-BLK attempted to [[Death/Legends|kill]] the Seville matriarch during one match, leaping out of the pit to attack her. Her son, [[Yearo Seville]], intervened by ionizing the droid. As a result, Yearo sent MdZ-BLK to a rival [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]], the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Gorbu Dalo]], with the impression that the droid would eventually build enough hatred for the Hutt and murder him.<ref name="Cracken" />

After MdZ-BLK eventually killed the Hutt, he still sought to kill the Sevilles. The MdZ series droid [[Programmer/Legends|reprogrammed]] a group of protocol droids to steal a [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] from a [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] family. The [[Starship/Legends|freighter]] was then converted into a large [[Bomb/Legends|bomb]] into the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] where the [[Seville family compound]] resided. Successfully eliminating the Sevilles, MdZ-BLK went on to travel [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] until he encountered the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Technician/Legends|maintenance specialist]] [[Aimi Loto]]. The two partnered and acted as [[Saboteur/Legends|saboteurs]] against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. They traveled from [[Star system/Legends|system]] to system [[Sabotage droid/Legends|sabotaging]] Imperial droids to later destroy Imperial equipment and personnel. They moved every few [[Standard month/Legends|months]] so their sabotage could not be linked back to them.<ref name="Cracken" />

===Adventures with Loto===
At some point Loto and MdZ-BLK reprogrammed protocol droid attendants for individuals from over twenty [[Sector/Legends|sectors]], with each one being a guest to [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Nile Owen]]'s [[Nile Owen's daughter|daughter's]] [[Marriage/Legends|wedding]]. They also traveled to<ref name="Cracken" /> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="Karvoss">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> [[Karvoss II]]. There, they met [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] when he needed his [[Unidentified R2 unit (Airen Cracken)|R2-series astromech droid]] repaired. During the transaction, Cracken spoke with MdZ-BLK, though when Loto learned the general was traveling to the wedding of Owen's [[Gender|daughter]], she warned him of the protocol droids while the MdZ series droid laughed loudly.<ref name="Cracken" />

==Behind the scenes==
MdZ-BLK was introduced in a section written by [[Chuck Truett]] and illustrated by [[Mike Jackson]] in ''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]'', a [[1994]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] sourcebook for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="Cracken" />
